_comment: Published IN-STATE tuition and required fees at PUBLIC institutions (IPEDS IC*_AY) beside state education appropriations per full-time-equivalent student (SHEEO SHEF), both in constant 2024 dollars -- tuition deflated by CPI-U from the BLS API, appropriations by SHEEO's own HECA index, which is an index and therefore DIVIDES. TUITION HERE IS A PUBLISHED RATE: the sticker before any discount, waiver, scholarship or aid, so it is what a student is quoted and not what the average student pays. Two series moving apart is a substitution PATTERN, NOT A DEMONSTRATED CAUSE -- legislatures set one and boards the other, both responding to enrolment, cost and politics at once. THE PERIOD DECIDES THE STORY, so always give the window: the substitution is a 2008-2012 event, and across 2011-2023 it RUNS THE OTHER WAY -- median state appropriations per FTE rose 11.2% in real terms, median in-state sticker rose 2.5%, and median NET PRICE FELL 6.6% with 35 of 51 states down. 'Students pay more while states pay less' describes the crash years, not the decade after them. NET PRICE is the better measure of what is actually paid and is a DIFFERENT population and basis from the sticker beside it: first-time full-time undergraduates receiving aid, cost of attendance including living costs, minus grant aid. Public institutions only, because in-state tuition is a public-sector concept.
